name: Elead
overview: Elead was a male member of the tribe of Ephraim, known primarily as the grandson of Ephraim. His life is briefly noted in Scripture, where it is recorded that he was killed by the men of Gath. His mention underscores the ongoing conflicts between Israel and surrounding peoples during the period.
namesAndTitles: The name Elead means 'G-d has testified,' reflecting a theologically significant meaning rooted in the Hebrew name El. This proper name, found in 1 Chronicles 7:21, was not given directly by God but carries a meaningful declaration of divine testimony.
familyAndRelationships: Elead is explicitly identified as the grandson of Ephraim, the son of Joseph, situating him within the prominent tribe of Ephraim. Beyond this, Scripture does not record additional family relationships for Elead.
scriptureSignificance: Elead's mention in Scripture highlights his place within the lineage of Ephraim, a key tribe in Israel's history. His death at the hands of the men of Gath reflects the hostile environment Israel faced from neighboring peoples. Though his role is brief, Elead's story contributes to the broader biblical narrative of tribal identity and conflict.
